items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: I saw a friend... we started talking about Max Steiner and Ray Heindorf and all of these people that I lived with every day

ctx.x: Yes. He absorbed everything around him from all the different kinds of music he listened to.

Well you know I lived in Hollywood, in fact I saw — I was conducting in the south last night and I saw a friend, a gentleman that I hadn’t seen for a long time who was kind of an assistant director for Warner Brothers in the golden days. And we started talking about Max Steiner and Ray Heindorf and all of these people that I lived with every day, and never really knew how important they were and what a stroke they put on not only my life but the life of America. You know, Alfred Newman at Fox. And I worked for —…
Didn’t you make your way to Hollywood with a chance encounter with Judy Garland?
